WGU Business Management: how Sophia and Study.com fit the 110-unit degree

DegreeSteps’s reviewed starting proposal for WGU Business Management assigns 69 of the degree’s 110 competency units to published Sophia and Study.com options, with 41 assigned to WGU. Here is what that mix means, which courses illustrate it, and how to adapt it to work you already have.

Use the right program and the right units

This example applies to the Business Management B.S. curriculum associated with the May 2026 transfer agreements and the institutional policies reviewed in November 2026. It is a 110-competency-unit degree. A different WGU degree or catalog can have a different structure, so an older 120-credit spreadsheet should not be pasted into this plan.

WGU’s competency units describe the receiving degree. They are not a universal conversion formula for every outside course. For example, a source course can satisfy a WGU requirement worth a different number of units. The source course identity, original credit amount, and WGU award belong in separate fields.

The starting proposal assumes no existing student courses. If you have previous college work, exams, or eligible credentials, bring those records into the comparison before buying a new subscription. A similar course title alone does not establish an equivalent award.

What the 69-and-41 mix includes

The saved default selects 43 receiving WGU competency units from Sophia options and 26 from Study.com options. Those total 69 outside units. Another selection of published options may divide the providers differently; 43 and 26 describe this proposal rather than a rule requiring every student to buy that exact mix.

The remaining 41 units are assigned to WGU coursework in this route. That is not a claim that all 41 can never have another transfer option. It is the university work left in the supported starting proposal. Keep the capstone and any other required WGU work visible while comparing alternatives.

Several actual course placements make the idea clearer

The important part is the requirement each course fills. The examples below come from the selected starting proposal. They illustrate why the plan needs receiving course codes and exact source identities, rather than a shopping list of vaguely related business subjects.

A source course should not be reused to create separate credit awards for two requirements when WGU’s rules prohibit that reuse. The plan accounts for that restriction. The same caution applies when you have already earned a course through another source: avoid buying a second course that fills a requirement already covered.

Choose the provider sequence before paying

Start by identifying courses already covered by your records. Next, decide which remaining requirements can use the selected provider’s courses. Group applicable courses into a realistic subscription period, accounting for concurrent-course limits, assignments, grading, and your weekly study time.

Current provider profiles distinguish Study.com College Saver from College Saver Pro, because course inclusion matters. A less expensive tier is not a saving if it omits the course needed for your WGU requirement. The same subscription can have a different effective cost per completed course for two students with different schedules.

You can also compare another published option in the full plan. The practical question is whether the change reduces your own remaining work or cost while keeping the exact WGU requirement satisfied. A provider’s broad partnership badge cannot answer that on its own.

Plan WGU terms separately from outside subscriptions

The reviewed November 2026 institutional catalog lists $3,850 tuition and a $200 resource fee per six-month Business Management term, totaling $4,050 for those term charges. It also lists a separate $65 application fee. Outside coursework, optional expenses, financial aid, and your number of remaining WGU terms are separate.

A six-month billing period is not a guarantee that 41 remaining units can be finished in six months. Your readiness, assessments, available study time, and the school’s requirements affect the calendar. Compare a scenario using explicit assumptions rather than treating one term as the price of the entire degree.

WGU’s transfer submission rules also make sequencing important. Arrange the required records and evaluation before the initial term under the current policy. Taking an outside course after starting is not a substitute for satisfying the school’s prestart transfer process.

Make the proposal yours

Open the complete plan, keep or change supported course choices, and add your existing learning. Look at each requirement alongside the proposed provider and the university work still left. You can compare another degree using the same original courses without rewriting your history.

The goal is a route you can execute: a clear list of applicable outside courses, a realistic subscription sequence, and visible remaining WGU coursework. Start with the reviewed proposal, then refine the parts that depend on your own records and schedule.
